documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

55-year-old man transferring care. Former construction supervisor, out on medical disability for several years; Medicare by disability with a supplemental plan. Brought a partial printout from his previous primary care office; full records requested today.

HPI / background:
- Hepatitis C, found around 2006 on routine bloodwork at the old practice. Never treated. Old printouts show transaminases running high for years and drifting up over roughly the last decade.
- Diabetes on insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime for a few years. He is not sure what type he was told he had; no oral agents on the list and none he remembers. Checks fingersticks most mornings, typically 110s to 140s, no lows he knows of. Type not clear from what he brought. Will treat as insulin-requiring diabetes, type unclassified, until records are in.
- Upper abdominal pain: has had bouts of it on and off for several years, comes and goes, none for a while and none today. No workup for it that he recalls.
- Alcohol: drinks regularly, more on weekends. He knows it is a problem with the liver and says he wants to cut back but is not ready to quit outright.

PMH: chronic hepatitis C; diabetes on basal insulin.
PSH: appendectomy age 12 (1976); cholecystectomy age 45 (2009). No records of either.
Meds: insulin glargine 24 units subcut at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father had alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis, died at 65. Mother has type 2 diabetes. Brother has chronic pancreatitis.
SH: lives in Northampton. Former smoker, about 30 pack-years, quit around 2016. Alcohol as above. No other substances.

ROS: no abdominal pain currently, no jaundice, no dark urine, no change in stools, no chest pain or dyspnea, no polyuria.

Exam: BP 112/69, HR 72, T 36.9, SpO2 97% RA. Wt 81.0 kg, Ht 177.6 cm, BMI 25.7.
Well appearing, no jaundice or scleral icterus. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ and laparoscopic scars, no palpable liver edge or spleen tip, no distension. No edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament sensation intact bilaterally.

A/P:
1. Chronic hepatitis C, untreated, with longstanding transaminase elevation. CMP, CBC, INR today. Discussed that alcohol is the single biggest thing he can change for his liver. Old records requested.
2. Diabetes on basal insulin, type unclassified. A1c today. Continue glargine 24 units qhs. Meter strips and pen needles on file with pharmacy.
3. Alcohol use disorder. Brief counselling done; he agreed to try cutting back on weekday drinking and to talk about it again next visit. Offered more support, declined for now.
4. Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit within 15 years: low-dose CT lung screening ordered.
5. Health maintenance: no colonoscopy ever, referral placed. PCV13 and Tdap today (no record of a prior tetanus booster). Flu, shingles and hepatitis A/B series to start at a nurse visit next month. HIV screen with labs. Lipids and urine albumin today.

Return in 3 months.

We will recheck the liver numbers in a few months. The most helpful thing for your liver is still cutting down on the alcohol, like we talked about.

See you in December.

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST
Indication: steatorrhea, weight loss, intermittent upper abdominal pain.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 02/24/2021
Referred by: primary care, for greasy stools and weight loss.

HPI: 56-year-old man with untreated hepatitis C and insulin-treated diabetes. For the last three weeks his stools have been loose, bulky and foul, and he notices an oily sheen left on the water. Over the past month he has lost weight without trying, although he is eating as much as ever. No fever, no blood per rectum, no travel. He describes upper abdominal pain that has come and gone for years. He drinks now and then and says he has cut back a lot over the past year.

PMH: chronic hepatitis C (about 2006, untreated); diabetes on basal insulin.
PSH: appendectomy (age 12), cholecystectomy (age 45).
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: brother with chronic pancreatitis; father with alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis; mother with type 2 diabetes.
SH: former smoker, 30 pack-years. Alcohol as above.

Exam: comfortable. No jaundice. No palmar erythema, spider nevi or other cutaneous signs of chronic liver disease seen. Abdomen soft, mildly tender in the epigastrium, no guarding or rebound, no palpable mass.

Labs today: Hgb 12.6, MCV 92, platelets 167. Albumin 3.2 (low). AST 78, ALT 59, bilirubin 0.9, creatinine 0.9.
CT abdomen/pelvis today: atrophic pancreas with coarse calcification and irregular ductal dilation; liver without focal lesion.

Assessment:
1. Chronic pancreatitis with exocrine pancreatic insufficiency. The CT is diagnostic and the steatorrhea with weight loss reflects exocrine failure. Alcohol and family history both likely contribute.
2. Diabetes: in light of chronic calcific pancreatitis, his insulin-requiring diabetes is best classified as diabetes secondary to chronic pancreatitis (type 3c, pancreatogenic). Continue current insulin through primary care.
3. Mild anemia and low albumin, likely nutritional in the setting of malabsorption.
4. Chronic hepatitis C, followed by primary care.

Plan:
- Start pancrelipase (Creon) 36,000 lipase units by mouth with each meal and each snack, taken with the first bites. Prescription sent.
- Complete alcohol abstinence advised strongly; he agreed to stop.
- Weight and stool response at follow-up; primary care to monitor weight, albumin and glucose.

Thank you for involving us.
Gastroenterology

documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 08/23/2021
(Record forwarded to primary care 08/26/2021 after final labs posted.)

Chief complaint: dizzy spells before meals.

HPI: 57-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis and exocrine insufficiency, type 3c diabetes on basal insulin, previously worked up for malabsorption and low albumin. Over the past few weeks he has had episodes of lightheadedness, a racing heartbeat and sweating that come on before meals, especially late morning when breakfast is small, and go away once he eats. This morning had a spell while doing yard work and came in. No loss of consciousness, no chest pain, no focal weakness.

PMH: chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency; type 3c diabetes; chronic hepatitis C; low albumin.
PSH: appendectomy; cholecystectomy.
Meds: pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, 30 pack-years. Alcohol use disorder, no alcohol since February 2021.

Vitals: BP 124/76, HR 88, RR 16, T 36.7, SpO2 98% on arrival; stable throughout.
Exam: alert, comfortable after juice. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Neuro nonfocal. No remarkable findings.

Results:
- Fasting glucose 60 mg/dL on arrival (before oral glucose).
- Hemoglobin A1c 6.2%.
- C-peptide 0.5 ng/mL (reference 1.1-4.4), low. Resulted 08/25.
- Serum insulin: reported low. Resulted 08/25. Note: this insulin immunoassay may not detect glargine, so a low result does not exclude exogenous basal insulin.

ED course: given oral glucose and a meal; repeat fingerstick normal. Observed several hours without recurrence.

Assessment: insulin-induced hypoglycemia. Low glucose on basal insulin with a low C-peptide, so no excess of his own insulin; fits glargine acting during long gaps between meals.

Disposition: discharged home.

Admitted: 02/27/2025 via emergency department. Discharged: 03/04/2025.
Service: Gastroenterology.

Reason for admission: a week of steady epigastric pain boring through to the back, with vomiting, worse each day.

History: 60-year-old man with chronic calcific pancreatitis and exocrine insufficiency since 2021, type 3c diabetes on glargine, untreated chronic hepatitis C, treated distal esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (2024) and follicular lymphoma (2023), hairy cell leukemia in remission. No alcohol since 2021.
Allergies: NKDA.
Home medications: pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.

On admission: vital signs stable (BP 128/78, HR 92, afebrile, SpO2 97%). Epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding.
Labs: Na 140, K 4.0, Cl 108, HCO3 15, BUN 18, creatinine 1.0, glucose 90, calcium 9.2, anion gap 17. Albumin 2.7, AST 82, ALT 61, bilirubin 0.8. Hgb 11.7, WBC 6.4.

Diagnosis: pancreatic duct leak (disruption in the tail) with small adjacent collection, in chronic pancreatitis.

Hospital course: managed without endoscopic or surgical intervention. Bowel rest, IV fluids, IV antiemetics and analgesia. Glargine continued with glucose checks; dextrose-containing fluids while NPO; no hypoglycemia. Discharge medications: unchanged. Pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.

CARDIAC SURGERY CONSULTATION
Date of consult: 02/23/2026

Asked to evaluate for surgery: Enterococcus faecalis aortic valve endocarditis with new first-degree AV block.

Data: blood cultures 3 of 3 positive for E. faecalis, ampicillin susceptible; cultures from 02/22 no growth to date. TTE 02/19: aortic valve vegetation, moderate AR, normal LV size and function. TEE 02/20: vegetation about 8 mm on the aortic valve, moderate AR, no abscess or other perivalvular extension. ECG: PR 260 ms (170 ms in 2024); daily ECGs since admission show no lengthening and no higher-grade block.

Background: chronic hepatitis C with hepatic dysfunction, chronic pancreatitis, type 3c diabetes, treated esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, lymphoma and hairy cell leukemia.

Assessment: the conduction change raises concern for perivalvular spread, but TEE shows none, cultures cleared within 3 days of antibiotics, the PR interval is stable, the vegetation is under 10 mm and the left ventricle is preserved.

Recommendation: medical therapy, no surgery at this time. Continue daily ECGs while inpatient; reconsult for progression of block, heart failure, embolic events or persistent bacteremia.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary — Cardiology
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 02/19/2026 via emergency department to the cardiac intensive care unit. Transferred to the cardiology ward 02/23/2026. Discharged: 03/03/2026.

Presenting problem: a week of fevers, malaise, fatigue and mild shortness of breath.

History: 61-year-old man with untreated chronic hepatitis C, chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency, type 3c diabetes on glargine, follicular lymphoma in remission, distal esophageal squamous cell carcinoma treated with chemoradiation in 2024 without recurrence, and hairy cell leukemia in remission. No alcohol since 2021.
Allergies: NKDA.
Home medications: pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.

Admission findings: T 38.8 C (101.8 F), BP 120/72, HR 96, RR 18, SpO2 97% on room air. Early diastolic murmur along the left sternal border in full expiration. Lungs clear.
Labs: Hgb 10.2, WBC 12.2, platelets 165. Albumin 2.8. Creatinine 0.84.
ECG: sinus rhythm, first-degree AV block, PR 260 ms, new against 2024 baseline (170 ms).

Microbiology: 3 of 3 blood culture sets from 02/19 grew Enterococcus faecalis, ampicillin susceptible (reported 02/20). Repeat cultures 02/22: no growth at 5 days.
Imaging: TTE 02/19: aortic valve vegetation, moderate aortic regurgitation, normal LV size and systolic function. TEE 02/20: aortic valve vegetation approximately 8 mm, moderate regurgitation, no abscess, fistula or other perivalvular extension.

Diagnosis: infective endocarditis of the native aortic valve due to Enterococcus faecalis, complicated by new first-degree AV block.

Course: started IV ampicillin plus ceftriaxone on 02/19. Defervesced by 02/23. Monitored in the CICU on telemetry until 02/23; daily ECGs with stable PR, no progression. Cardiac surgery consulted because of the conduction change and advised medical therapy given no perivalvular extension on TEE, cultures cleared within 3 days and a stable PR. Glargine continued with point-of-care glucose; no hypoglycemia. Right arm PICC placed 03/02 for outpatient therapy.

Discharge plan:
- IV ampicillin plus ceftriaxone through home infusion, to complete 6 weeks from culture clearance on 02/22/2026: last dose 04/05/2026.
- Weekly CBC and BMP through home infusion.
- Amoxicillin 2 g by mouth 30-60 minutes before dental procedures, from now on.
- Primary care within 1 week; cardiology clinic with repeat TTE in about 10 weeks.
- Return for fever, worsening shortness of breath, palpitations, fainting, or PICC problems.
Discharge medications: as above plus home pancrelipase and glargine unchanged.

Transitional care visit after admission 2/19-3/3 for Enterococcus faecalis aortic valve endocarditis with new first-degree AV block. Discharge summary and cardiac surgery consult reviewed. RN contact 3/4.

On home IV ampicillin plus ceftriaxone via right arm PICC since discharge; last dose 4/5. No fevers at home. Energy low but improving. Breathing back to normal. No palpitations, no lightheadedness or fainting. Eating; Creon with meals and snacks.
Sugars: fasting 100-140, no lows.
Medications reconciled: IV ampicillin and ceftriaxone through 4/5; amoxicillin 2 g before dental procedures; Creon; glargine 24 units.

Exam: BP 126/82, HR 76, T 36.7, SpO2 98%, Wt 60.2 kg.
Heart regular, soft early diastolic murmur at left sternal border. Lungs clear.
PICC right upper arm: dressing clean and dry, no redness, tenderness or swelling, arm not swollen.
No splinter hemorrhages. No edema.

A/P:
1. E. faecalis aortic valve endocarditis on IV therapy: afebrile, PICC site clean. CBC and BMP today. Home infusion labs weekly. Cardiology with TTE in May.
2. First-degree AV block: no symptoms; cardiology following ECGs. Call for dizziness or fainting.
3. Dental prophylaxis: amoxicillin 2 g before dental work from now on; he will tell his dentist.
4. Type 3c diabetes: glargine unchanged.
